candidate.claim: Repeated greedy 'commit if held-out score improves' can accumulate false/harmful self-edits; PACE uses paired anytime-valid sequential evidence to control per-candidate false commits under optional stopping and substantially reduces spurious edits in the tested prompt-evolution setup.

primary_source.title: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents
primary_source.author: Zayx Shawn
primary_source.access_note: The current web environment exposed the arXiv primary abstract/metadata but disabled direct arXiv full-text/PDF fetch. All headline quantitative claims below are stated in that primary abstract; detailed table/theorem internals were not independently re-extracted from the arXiv full text in this audit.

mechanism.detail: PACE (Paired Anytime-valid Commit Evaluation) compares each candidate with the incumbent on identical instances and commits only when a testing-by-betting e-process accumulates decisive evidence, with early stopping.
mechanism.guarantee_scope: The primary abstract explicitly states control of each candidate's false-commit probability at a user-set level under optional stopping and explicitly labels this a per-decision guarantee.

genuine_improvement_among_noise.PACE_result: commits the real improvement and essentially nothing else
genuine_improvement_among_noise.performance: matches greedy held-out accuracy with sharply lower variance

no_real_gain.worst_reported_degradation: 4.9 points on the most fragile agent

scope_clarifications: The statistical guarantee is per candidate/decision, not a run-level familywise guarantee across an unbounded or endogenous lineage of accepted edits. The worker already states this correctly and downstream consumers must preserve it.

The demonstrated system-level scope is prompt evolution on Qwen2.5 0.5B-3B over three benchmarks. Transfer to skill/code/topology self-modification, changing evaluation distributions, or endogenous proposal processes is not established by these headline experiments.
The reported false/harmful commit rates are properties of the paper's proposal/evaluation regimes and dev-set setup; they are not universal base rates for greedy acceptance.

PACE's per-decision anytime-validity does not itself solve repeated reuse of a fixed evaluation distribution at the lineage level, model-selection across many candidate gates, or edit-induced distribution shift. A separate global/accounting layer would need its own guarantee.

Because direct arXiv full-text/PDF access was disabled in this audit environment, detailed theorem assumptions, exact betting construction, replicate counts and table cells remain a primary-full-text verification frontier even though all O_FEED headline numbers are present in the primary abstract.
